problem: A linear system of ODEs has an equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}.$ One of the nullclines of the system has the equation $y=2x-3$ in the corresponding phase space. The system is then shifted using $u=x-{x}^{∗}.$ Which of the following is **guaranteed** to be a nullcline of the shifted system?

feedback.problem: A linear system of ODEs has the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}=[1,\,-1]^{T}.$ Two linearly independent eigenvectors of the system's matrix are ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}.$ After shifting using $u=x-{x}^{∗},$ the system becomes ${u}^{′}=Au.$ Which of the following is **guaranteed** to be an eigenvector of the matrix $A?$
feedback.worked_solution:
After shifting a linear system, the eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors remain unchanged.

Thus, the matrix $A$ in the shifted system has the same eigenvectors as the system's matrix in the original coordinates. These eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ or any nonzero vectors that are parallel to them.

Among the given options, the only vector that is nonzero and is guaranteed to be parallel to either ${v}_{1}$ or ${v}_{2}$ is the vector $-{v}_{2}.$
